triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale scopes a recurrence claim to a work unit -- 'a collocation that recurs elsewhere in this part (25:13's harvest day, 27:10's day of disaster)' -- where the register law requires row prose to describe the text and cross-row references to be verse-anchored; a writer part is a process object, so TEST 1 is failed. TEST 2 (E-18 arm) re-derived from bytes: the claim is TRUE. The token בְּי֣וֹם (spliced oshb:Prov.25.19) stands word-bound in 10 verses book-wide (6:34, 11:4, 12:16, 24:10, 25:13, 25:19, 25:20, 27:1, 27:10, 27:15) and in 6 verses inside 25:1-27:27 (25:13, 25:19, 25:20, 27:1, 27:10, 27:15), so both named recurrences are byte-real, though the part-scope silently passes over 27:1 and 27:15. The seam judgement behind it also holds: the staged catchword inventory records 25:19|25:20 as one of ch 25's 7 shared content-token pairs with that single token, and the row correctly refuses it as cohesion evidence. A true claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The recurrence of the day-of collocation is scoped to a writer part instead of a verse range, and carries no digit-bearing sweep citation.
findings.grounds: The prose reads 'recurs elsewhere in this part'; the row's own governing literary unit is its parent_collection C5 Prov.25.1-Prov.29.27, and the part range 25:1-27:27 is not a text boundary (it bisects C5). Re-swept: בְּי֣וֹם (spliced oshb:Prov.25.19) is word-bound in 10 verses book-wide and 6 verses in 25:1-27:27; both digits are absent from the row. Nothing about the seam changes -- the shared token is disclosed and correctly refused.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: replace 'recurs elsewhere in this part (25:13's harvest day, 27:10's day of disaster)' with a verse-anchored, digit-bearing form, e.g. 'recurs at 25:13, 27:1, 27:10 and 27:15 (word-bound sweep of the skeleton token: 6 verses in 25:1-27:27, 10 book-wide)'.

findings.claim: The exclusivity claim 'shares only the common formulaic phrase' carries no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation, though it re-derives as true.
findings.grounds: oshb:Prov.25.19 and oshb:Prov.25.20 share exactly one exact-skeleton token, בְּי֣וֹם (spliced oshb:Prov.25.19); the staged catchword inventory independently lists 25:19|25:20 as a shared-content-token pair whose single shared token is that word, and reproduction of the inventory's object returns 7 shared pairs in ch 25 with no other pair touching 25:19. The claim is byte-true; the book law requires every only-class claim to carry an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit, and none is present.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: add the digit and object, e.g. 'shares exactly 1 skeleton token with 25:20'.

triggers.grounds: Two work-unit references in boundary_rationale -- 'the same pair attested again, non-adjacently, at 26:21 and 27:15 in this part' and '21:9, which lies outside this part' -- plus the same frame in observed_substrate_signals ('recurs at 3 non-adjacent verses in this part'). TEST 1 failed: the scope named is a writer part, not a text range. TEST 2 re-derived from bytes: every claim is TRUE. oshb:Prov.25.24 carries the inline unpointed ketiv מדונים immediately before the pointed qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (pmarks_Prov.json kq: 1 note at that verse, single-witness WLC), and the identical inline pair stands at oshb:Prov.26.21 and oshb:Prov.27.15 (kq: 1 each), so the digit 3 is byte-true inside 25:1-27:27; book-wide the same inline pair stands in 5 verses (21:19, 23:29, 25:24, 26:21, 27:15), which the part-scope conceals. The 21:9 comparison is honestly hedged and no tier was overclaimed: 21:9 differs from 25:24 in its infinitive and carries NO ketiv/qere note in the inventory, so 'near-identical' is exact. The tov digit re-derives too: 16 verses whose first skeleton token is ט֗וֹב (staged inventory count_object), 25:24 among them. True claims in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The ketiv/qere recurrence digit and the 21:9 comparison are scoped to a writer part rather than to a verse range or to the row's own collection.
findings.grounds: The row's parent_collection is C5 Prov.25.1-Prov.29.27; the part range 25:1-27:27 is a work unit that bisects it, and 21:9 lies outside C5 as well (C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16), so the substantive point survives the register violation intact. The scoped digit is byte-true (3 verses inside 25:1-27:27: 25:24, 26:21, 27:15, each carrying the inline ketiv מדונים with the qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים spliced from oshb:Prov.25.24 and each recorded in pmarks_Prov.json kq), but the book-wide digit for the same object is 5 (adds 21:19 and 23:29) and is nowhere stated. The K/Q inside the row's own quoted span is properly disclosed, so this is register and scope only.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale / observed_substrate_signals field repair only: replace both 'this part' scopes with explicit verse ranges and give the book-wide digit, e.g. 'the identical inline ketiv/qere pair stands at 26:21 and 27:15 within 25:1-29:27 (5 verses book-wide: 21:19, 23:29, 25:24, 26:21, 27:15)'; and 'at 21:9, outside this collection (C2 10:1-22:16)'.

triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'No cluster candidate was found in the adjacency sweep for this part' -- a process reference (the sweep) inside a work-unit scope, failing TEST 1 twice over: the field narrates the workflow instead of describing the text. TEST 2 re-derived from bytes: the underlying judgement is sound under the campaign's defined object -- the staged catchword inventory counts adjacent-verse pairs sharing at least one stoplist-filtered content token, and reproduction of that object returns 7/4/1 shared pairs for chs 25/26/27, matching the inventory exactly, with neither 25:24|25:25 nor 25:25|25:26 among them. As literally worded at the unfiltered tier the absence claim is false (see the finding). True judgement in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The rejected_alternative narrates a sweep over a writer part instead of stating a text-anchored rival.
findings.grounds: The field's whole content is 'No cluster candidate was found in the adjacency sweep for this part.' The register law bans process narration and work-unit scopes in row prose and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored; the row's own neighbours are 25:24 and 25:26, both already in boundary_evidence_refs, so a verse-anchored rewrite loses nothing.
findings.proposed_change: strongest_rejected_alternative field repair only: state the rival in text terms, e.g. 'Clustering with 25:24 or 25:26 was rejected: neither neighbour shares a content token with this verse.'

findings.claim: 'Unlinked by skeleton token to either neighbour' is false at the unfiltered exact-token skeleton tier: 25:24 and 25:25 carry the same preposition token.
findings.grounds: The spliced token עַל (oshb:Prov.25.24) and the spliced token עַל (oshb:Prov.25.25) are the same exact skeleton token, so the row's 'unlinked by skeleton token to either neighbor' and its observed_substrate_signals 'skeleton comparison against both neighbors returns no shared token' are literally false at the tier they name. Under the object the staged inventory actually defines -- adjacent-verse pairs sharing at least one content token, skeleton tier, len>=2, stoplist-filtered -- the claim is TRUE: reproduction of that object returns exactly the inventory's 7/4/1 shared pairs for chs 25/26/27 and 25:24|25:25 is not among them. It is in fact one of only three adjacent pairs in chs 25-27 that share a token unfiltered but not under the inventory's object (with 25:6|25:7 and 26:1|26:2). Both occurrences are maqaf-joined in MT and stand as separate tokens only because the staged extract serializes maqaf as space, so no cohesion follows and the atomic span is unaffected; the shortfall is that the row names 'skeleton token' where the swept object is the stoplist-filtered content token. The same shorthand is used by the neighbouring rows, so the class may be corpus-wide rather than row-local.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale / observed_substrate_signals field repair only: name the object, e.g. 'shares no content token with either neighbour (the only unfiltered overlap with 25:24 is the maqaf-bound preposition)'.

triggers.grounds: Both flagged matches scope a count and an exclusivity claim to a writer part -- 'Unlike the 5 other comparative similes in this part' in boundary_rationale and 'the 5 other comparative similes in this part (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:8, 27:19)' in strongest_rejected_alternative -- failing TEST 1. TEST 2 re-derived from bytes: the enumeration is exact. The apodosis marker כֵּֽן (spliced oshb:Prov.26.19), swept word-bound at skeleton tier, stands in exactly 6 verses inside 25:1-27:27 (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 26:19, 27:8, 27:19), so the 5 named are precisely the complement of the row's own verse, and each of the 5 carries both the particle-marked protasis and its apodosis inside one verse. The exclusivity claim is stronger than the row states: of the 6 verses in the book that open with that marker (1:19, 6:29, 11:19, 24:14, 26:19, 30:20), only 26:19's preceding verse opens with the comparison particle -- oshb:Prov.26.18 opens כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ and oshb:Prov.26.19 opens כֵּֽן אִ֭ישׁ -- while the other five protases (1:18, 6:28, 11:18, 24:13, 30:19) carry no such particle, so 26:18-19 is the only split particle-and-apodosis comparison BOOK-wide, not merely inside the part. The digit 5, by contrast, is scope-dependent (see the finding). True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The simile count and the uniqueness claim are scoped to an unnamed writer part; the count is scope-dependent, so the register cure must substitute an explicit range rather than delete the qualifier.
findings.grounds: Inside 25:1-27:27 the intra-verse particle-and-apodosis similes are 26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:8, 27:19 (5, exactly as named), and the same digit holds inside the row's parent_collection C5 Prov.25.1-Prov.29.27 (28:2 carries the marker but not a comparative protasis). Book-wide the same object returns 6 verses, adding oshb:Prov.10.26, whose apodosis pivots at כֵּ֥ן. So a naive register purge that simply dropped 'in this part' would leave a byte-false digit. The uniqueness half of the claim survives at every scope: 26:18-19 is the only place in Prov where a particle-marked protasis and its verse-initial apodosis marker sit in different verses. The seam itself is untouched and rests on the owner-ratified reading of a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning two verses as one single_proverb unit.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale / strongest_rejected_alternative field repair only: replace 'in this part' with the explicit range, e.g. 'the 5 other comparative similes inside 25:1-29:27 (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:8, 27:19)', and state the uniqueness at its true scope: 'the only place in the book where the comparison particle and its resolving apodosis sit in different verses'.

findings.claim: An English run in boundary_rationale reproduces the WEB text of 26:18 verbatim apart from its initial capital and terminal comma, but is presented in straight quotes with no web: ref in the field.
findings.grounds: WEB Prov.26.18 reads “Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,” (web:Prov.26.18, staged verse_map_web.json); the row's run is 'like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death'. The book-wide convention reserves curly double quotes for WEB text and requires an inline web: ref in the same field, with straight quotes signalling row wording, so the provenance of the run is mis-signalled -- a reader cannot tell the witness from the writer's gloss. The Hebrew claim it illustrates is independently byte-true: oshb:Prov.26.18 runs כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ plus three nominal complements with no finite verb, and the apodosis כֵּֽן אִ֭ישׁ opens oshb:Prov.26.19, so nothing rests on the English run.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: either curly-quote the run verbatim with web:Prov.26.18 in the same field, or replace it with a splice of oshb:Prov.26.18 plus a straight-quoted gloss.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale closes 'disclosed here only as background since 18:8 lies outside this part', scoping the duplicate to a writer part; TEST 1 failed. TEST 2 re-derived from bytes: the claim is TRUE and every digit in the row re-derives. Verse-initial דִּבְרֵ֣י (spliced oshb:Prov.26.22) stands at exactly 5 sites -- 12:6, 18:8, 26:22, 30:1, 31:1 -- matching the staged inventory's count_object 'verses whose first skeleton token is divrei', and the 19-verse total matches the contiguous-skeleton object the book law uses. The byte-identity claim is exact: the full pointed run of oshb:Prov.26.22 collates at tier byte against oshb:Prov.18.8, and the two verses' codepoint sequences are equal, so 'byte-identical' names the right tier. The נִ֭רְגָּן digit 4 reproduces under the contiguous-skeleton sweep the row names (16:28 carries the word with a conjunctive vav; word-bound the digit is 3), and 26:20 is byte-real as the nearest occurrence. The front-seam mark is correct: pmarks_Prov.json records PE at Prov.26.21, disclosed as petuchah, single-witness, corroborative only, with no conflation with the book's single SAMEKH at 24:22. 18:8 does lie outside the row's collection as well as outside the part. True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The duplicate at 18:8 is placed 'outside this part' where the governing unit is the row's own collection.
findings.grounds: The row's parent_collection is C5 Prov.25.1-Prov.29.27 and 18:8 sits in C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16, so the substantive disclosure is right but is framed by a work unit that is not a text boundary. No digit or seam depends on the frame: the byte-identity of oshb:Prov.26.22 with oshb:Prov.18.8 is verified at byte tier and carries no boundary consequence, exactly as the row says.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: replace 'lies outside this part' with 'lies outside this collection (C2 10:1-22:16)'.

findings.claim: The rejected_alternative rests the header rejection on what an inventory 'names', and that attribution does not match the staged artifact.
findings.grounds: The field reads 'the header inventory names only 30:1 and 31:1 as headers among the 19 divrei verses'. In the staged prov_device_inventory.json the only field literally called headers is a collection_seams map of eleven ref-to-text entries that INCLUDES Prov.26.22 (with 12:6, 18:8, 1:1, 1:6, 10:1, 22:17, 24:23, 25:1, 30:1, 31:1); the artifact carries no per-verse header status, and the ruling that 12:6, 18:8 and 26:22 are not headers comes from the book strategy, not from the inventory. Naming a tooling artifact in row prose is a register violation in its own right. The conclusion is nonetheless correct and text-supportable without the artifact: 26:22 stands mid-way inside C5, whose opening header verse is 25:1, and the verse is byte-identical to the proverb at 18:8 rather than a superscription, so nothing about the rejection or the span changes.
findings.proposed_change: strongest_rejected_alternative field repair only: drop the inventory reference and argue from the text, e.g. 'Reading 26:22 as a collection-opening header was rejected: it stands inside the collection opened at 25:1 and repeats the proverb of 18:8 word for word, where 30:1 and 31:1 open new collections.'

triggers.grounds: Two artifact references: boundary_rationale ends '(see that row for the rejected cluster)' and strongest_rejected_alternative is entirely 'See 27:3's row for the rejected shape-only cluster with this verse.' The register law bans positional row references outright and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored; 'that row' is bare-positional and '27:3's row' still points at the artifact rather than the text, so TEST 1 is failed and the rejected_alternative field carries no self-standing rival. TEST 2: the referenced claim is TRUE -- the 27:3 row does carry the rejected shape-only cluster with this verse, and the byte fact behind it re-derives exactly: oshb:Prov.27.3 and oshb:Prov.27.4 share no token at all, filtered or unfiltered, and ch 27 records exactly one shared adjacent pair in the staged catchword inventory (27:19|27:20), so the atomic span is right. True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: Both driver fields delegate to another row instead of stating the case in text terms, leaving the rejected_alternative without a rival of its own.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: '(see that row for the rejected cluster)'; strongest_rejected_alternative: 'See 27:3's row for the rejected shape-only cluster with this verse.' The substance is recoverable inside the row -- its own rationale already states the operative fact, that the verse is structurally close to 27:3 but shares no skeleton token with it, which re-derives as byte-true (zero shared tokens between oshb:Prov.27.3 and oshb:Prov.27.4 at any tier) -- so the repair is verbal only.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: drop '(see that row for the rejected cluster)' and restate the rival verse-anchored, e.g. 'Clustering with 27:3 on the shared gradation shape was rejected: the two verses share no lexical item, only an abstract rhetorical template.'

findings.claim: The row's only substrate signal anchors a Hebrew-side rhetorical-structure claim in WEB space, and the row splices no original-language text at all.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals reads 'web:Prov.27.4 climactic gradation complete within the verse', while every entry in boundary_evidence_refs is oshb: (Prov.27.3, Prov.27.4) and no Hebrew appears anywhere in the row -- the only row in this batch of which that is true. The campaign law requires the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim and holds WEB sentence facts at tier 4, never boundary evidence. The claim itself is byte-true on the MT side, so nothing load-bearing fails and the span stands: oshb:Prov.27.4 sets אַכְזְרִיּ֣וּת חֵ֭מָה beside וְשֶׁ֣טֶף אָ֑ף and closes with the interrogative וּמִ֥י יַ֝עֲמֹד, a three-step gradation complete inside the verse.
findings.proposed_change: observed_substrate_signals field repair only: re-anchor the signal to oshb:Prov.27.4 with a splice of the two nominal clauses and the closing interrogative, keeping the WEB rendering (if wanted) as an explicitly tier-4 corroboration.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale scopes a set-membership claim to a work unit -- 'joining the small set of this part's similes that resolve inside one verse, alongside 26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:19' -- and gives no digit at all; TEST 1 failed. TEST 2 re-derived from bytes: the enumeration is TRUE as scoped. Inside 25:1-27:27 the apodosis marker כֵּֽן (spliced oshb:Prov.27.8), swept word-bound at skeleton tier, stands in 6 verses (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 26:19, 27:8, 27:19); 26:19 is the one split case, leaving exactly the 5 intra-verse similes the row implies (itself plus the 4 named). 27:8 itself carries both halves inside the verse: oshb:Prov.27.8 opens כְּ֭צִפּוֹר and pivots at כֵּֽן. The row's contrast with the split simile at 26:18-19 is likewise byte-true and agrees with the 26:18-19 row's own account of the same set, so the two rows are coherent. True claim in workflow register, digit absent -> low.

findings.claim: The simile set is scoped to a writer part with no digit; as at the paired 26:18-19 row the count is scope-dependent, so the register cure must name a verse range rather than drop the qualifier.
findings.grounds: The implied digit is 5 (27:8 plus 26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:19) and is byte-true inside 25:1-27:27 and inside the row's parent_collection C5 Prov.25.1-Prov.29.27; book-wide the same object returns 6 verses, adding oshb:Prov.10.26. No digit or object is stated in the row, where the book law requires an adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation naming the object and unit for a set-membership claim of this kind. The seam is unaffected: 27:8 shares no content token with 27:7 or 27:9 (ch 27 has exactly one shared adjacent pair in the staged inventory, 27:19|27:20).
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: replace 'the small set of this part's similes that resolve inside one verse' with a digit-bearing, verse-anchored form, e.g. 'one of the 5 particle-and-apodosis similes that resolve inside a single verse within 25:1-29:27 (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:8, 27:19; 6 book-wide with 10:26)'.
